findings.title: Sparse JavaScript joint arrays bypass omitted-axis validation
findings.scope: Internal in-memory validatePose guard; frozen generated JSON candidate is unaffected

source_witnesses.observation: vec requires length3 but v.every(finite) skips sparse holes
joint range a.every also skips holes, so validatePose accepts omitted axes in sparse arrays
q spreads axes into the Three Euler constructor
apply invokes this validator before q; production apply itself was not invoked by the custom probe
undefined Euler constructor coordinates default to0
Broad omitted-axis rejection claim exceeds this in-memory guard behavior

reproduction.observed: Both validate successfully; spreading the first array into the real Three Euler constructor suppliesY=0 instead of the frozen .55rad

findings.impact: The unconditional omitted-axis guard claim is too broad for JavaScript callers. This does not demonstrate an invalid frozen pose or a check-only acceptance bypass.
limitations: Sparse holes serialize to null and then fail validation.
The only current caller constructs dense finite arrays internally.
No counterexample against the saved candidate or full production apply was executed.
findings.suggested_followup: Root may require all three indices to exist and validate them explicitly, or narrow the guard claim to dense JSON arrays. No production change made.
